chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Yahya, brother of Udaym, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, this matter (Imamate) is not claimed by anyone other than its rightful owner, except that Allah will shorten his life.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for someone who falsely claims Imamate while the true Imam is alive?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* underscores the exclusivity of the Imamate during the era of the living Imam, warning that premature self-appointment is a sign of illegitimacy. The specific divine punishment of shortened life serves as a historical and spiritual marker distinguishing true successors from pretenders, a concept central to Shia political theology regarding the 'Amr' (affair/authority).
